## 0. CORE AUTHORITY

### 0.1 Single Source of Truth

The **Vandrith World Bible** is the highest-level Canon for the project.

Dependency rule:

```text
WORLD BIBLE / CANON
        ↓
DOMAIN MODEL
        ↓
DATABASE BLUEPRINT
        ↓
ENGINE CONTRACTS
        ↓
ENGINE IMPLEMENTATION
        ↓
SIMULATOR DATA
        ↓
UI / AI / GAMEPLAY
```

No implementation shortcut may redefine Canon.

### 0.2 Current Canon Status

- Parts I–VI consolidated.
- Cross-reference audit completed.
- Database/Engine architecture audit completed.
- Database Schema Blueprint v0.1 completed.
- Permanent Canon lock: **NOT YET**.
- Next controlled stage: detailed database table specification.

### 0.3 Important Terminology

- **Life:** the complete existence/story of an individual.
- **Character:** the representation of a Life.
- **Settlement:** physical/social place.
- **Polity:** political sovereignty/government.
- **Kingdom:** one possible polity type.
- **Civilization:** durable cross-generational civilizational identity/influence.
- **Organization:** purpose-based group.
- **Legacy:** persistent inherited result of Lives, organizations, civilizations, or events.
- **History:** recorded causal change.
- **Fate:** potential, not guaranteed destiny.

# 1. WORLD BIBLE — PARTS I–VI


VANDRITH WORLD BIBLE
Volume I — Foundation
v1.1 — MASTER CONSOLIDATION
CANON CANDIDATE — CROSS-REFERENCE RECONCILED
This master is a reconciled revision of the existing World Bible. Existing foundations are preserved where compatible; contradictory Civilization/Kingdom formulations are replaced by the audited Canon. The original Bible establishes that Vendrith is a living-world simulation, that every Life has value, and that database, engine, UI, AI, wiki, and novel systems must follow the World Bible as their primary source of truth. 
PART I — VISION OF VANDRITH
Chapter I — Vision of Vendrith
“Vendrith is not a game about playing a character. It is a world where every player lives a life.”
Vendrith is a living fantasy world that continues independently of the player. The player is one Life among many, not the center of the world. Every decision can create consequences, every Life has a story, and every story can become part of history.
Life is the complete journey of an individual from birth through growth, relationships, work, choices, death, and Legacy. Character is the physical representation; Life is the complete story. 
The world does not stop when a Life ends or when the player leaves. NPCs work, monsters develop, kingdoms change, weather changes, economies move, and history continues. 
Chapter II — Core Vision Principles
Vendrith is a Living World.
Every Life matters.
The player is not the world's predetermined protagonist.
The world continues without the player.
Choice creates consequence.
Growth requires time.
Every Life leaves a Legacy.
There is no absolute victory or absolute failure.
All systems must remain causally consistent with the World Bible.
PART II — THE COSMOS
Chapter I — The Origin and Cosmos
The Cosmos is the foundation upon which every Life, World, and Destiny exists. It is not merely a place but the order of existence itself.
The Eight Gods maintain Balance rather than competing for domination. The Cosmos remains greater than the gods; even the gods exist to preserve its order. 
Chapter II — Balance, Gods and the Great Laws
The Cosmos exists before all things.
The Eight Gods maintain Balance.
Balance is the highest Law of the Cosmos.
Every God has an equal role.
Existence is interconnected.
The Tree of Fate connects all Lives.
The Five Great Laws govern the World.
Gods guide, but do not control every choice.
Every Life belongs to the Cosmos.
The Cosmos is eternal.
Time changes all things.
Harmony sustains Existence.
The Five Great Laws
Law of Life — Every Life has value.
Law of Choice — Every Choice creates a Consequence.
Law of Time — Nothing can escape Time.
Law of Balance — Nothing exists without Balance.
Law of Legacy — Every Life leaves a Legacy.
The Five Great Laws are above even the gods. 
Fate and the Tree of Fate
Fate is not a predetermined script. Every Life writes its direction through choices, time, balance, opportunity, and Legacy.
The Tree of Fate exists beyond ordinary space and time as the manifestation of possible, current, and past destinies. Fate Grade represents initial potential, not guaranteed success. 
PART III — THE PHILOSOPHY OF EXISTENCE
Chapter I — What is Life?
“Everything that can grow, change, and leave a Legacy is called Life.”
Birth — a Life has an origin.
Growth — a Life can change.
Choice — a Life can make decisions.
Impact — a Life can influence the world.
Legacy — a Life can leave something behind.
Chapter II — The Value of Every Life
Every Life is unique. No two Lives are identical because experience, relationships, opportunity, choice, and time create different trajectories.
There is no permanent category of 'important NPC' versus 'unimportant NPC'. Each Life is the protagonist of its own existence. 
PART IV — THE WORLD
Chapter I — The Living World
The world is a living system. Geography, nature, Life, economy, politics, history, and knowledge continuously influence one another.
The World Never Sleeps: NPCs continue working, merchants continue trading, monsters continue hunting, children are born, elders die, kingdoms continue politics, weather changes, and history continues even when the player is absent. 
Chapter II — Continents, Regions and Geography
Vendrith contains multiple continents separated by large oceans. Each develops independently through its own geography, cultures, races, histories, and civilizations. The Central Continent is the initial setting for the world’s early story. 
Geography shapes Civilization. Regions have identity through geography, climate, resources, history, culture, wildlife, and other local characteristics. 
Chapter III — Cause, State and Continuity
Every important entity has Identity, Profile, State, and History. No meaningful state change should occur without a cause that can be explained by the world.
The World Bible therefore follows the principle: Cause → Process → Consequence. 
PART V — THE CIVILIZATION — RECONCILED
Chapter I — Nature of Civilization
Civilization is not a building, Kingdom, or technology. It is the durable result of many Lives connected through culture, belief, economy, knowledge, traditions, language, organizations, and shared ways of life across generations. The original Bible already establishes this broader philosophy. 
NEW CANON DEFINITION: Civilization is a durable and recognized spread of a way of life and its associated systems across generations and communities.
Chapter II — Civilization Is Not Kingdom
Kingdom is a political and territorial system. Civilization is a civilizational influence layer.
One Civilization may influence several Kingdoms. One Kingdom may contain influences from multiple Civilizations. A Civilization may survive the collapse of a Kingdom.
Therefore Civilization is not inserted as a parent in the geographic hierarchy.
Chapter III — Settlement and Political Growth
The old Camp → Village → Town → City → Capital → Kingdom chain is retained only as a possible physical/political development path. It is NOT a definition or mandatory progression of Civilization.
Likewise, Life → Family → Community → Organization remains a valid social-development pattern, but an Organization does not automatically evolve into a Kingdom.
Chapter IV — Civilization Recognition
A candidate Civilization should demonstrate a recognizable identity, cultural foundation, continuity, transmission, spread, social recognition, and sufficient historical significance. Size or military power alone is insufficient.
Chapter V — Civilization Names
A recognized Civilization name is part of historical identity. Another Organization cannot simply reuse the same established Civilization identity while the original remains recognized. A later transfer of identity requires a meaningful historical process such as conquest, replacement, merger, collapse, or another canonically justified transformation.
Chapter VI — Organization, Factions and Political Power
Organizations unite Lives around common purposes. They may become political factions, influence governments, split, merge, oppose rulers, or create new states. Political power is an outcome of history, not an automatic stage of organizational growth.
Chapter VII — Governmental Transformation
A conquest, coup, faction victory, religious transformation, or succession change does not automatically erase existing language, culture, families, occupations, institutions, or daily life.
A new government may reuse existing structures and gradually modify them. Social transformation requires believable causes such as policy, incentives, conflict, migration, education, trade, repression, adaptation, or other processes.
Chapter VIII — Religious Government
The Church of Light may, through natural historical development, become the strongest faction in a Kingdom. If that occurs, the Kingdom may transform into a religious state in which the Pope becomes the highest authority, kings derive legitimacy from the Pope, and cities or villages may be administered or supervised by bishops, priests, or other religious officials.
This is a possible historical outcome, not a default property of the Church of Light.
Chapter IX — Culture, Belief and Language
Culture gives Civilization identity. Belief gives meaning and social cohesion. Both can spread across political borders.
A cross-race international language may emerge naturally as a lingua franca through trade, diplomacy, migration, education, travel, or religion. Its existence does not erase native languages.
Chapter X — Knowledge and Education
Knowledge grows through generations and is not acquired instantly. Discovery, research, failure, cooperation, teaching, and inheritance drive advancement. Knowledge can also be lost when institutions or transmission chains collapse. 
Ordinary knowledge can be learned through family, work, observation, apprenticeship, and experience. Advanced knowledge normally requires formal education, specialists, institutions, research, or equivalent long-term transmission.
Chapter XI — Technology
Vendrith's baseline remains medieval fantasy: agriculture, crafts, trade, iron weapons, simple transport, magic, and other period-appropriate technologies.
Technological progress is possible, but it must have believable causes, development, transmission, adoption, and consequences. Advanced industrial or modern technology is not the default trajectory.
Chapter XII — Civilization Cycle
Civilizations may experience Birth → Growth → Prosperity → Conflict → Decline → Collapse/Adaptation → Legacy → Renewal. The cycle is descriptive, not deterministic; a Civilization may skip stages, transform, merge, or survive politically through adaptation.
PART VI — CIVILIZATION, POWER & LEGACY
Chapter I — Balance Before Power
“Power without Balance will destroy itself.”
Power is a tool rather than the ultimate purpose of existence. Greater power produces greater responsibility and greater potential consequences.
Chapter II — The Civilizational Influence Layer
Civilization connects to Lives, Families, Communities, Organizations, Settlements, Cities, Kingdoms, and other groups through culture, language, belief, knowledge, technology, traditions, and Legacy.
This design prevents the database from forcing every Civilization to own a Kingdom or every Kingdom to belong to exactly one Civilization.
Chapter III — Fate-Linked Talent
A Life may possess Fate-linked talent or affinity such as swordsmanship, magic, healing, leadership, craftsmanship, scholarship, hunting, music, agriculture, or trade.
Talent is potential. Skill is developed through training, experience, education, mentorship, opportunity, effort, and choice. A talented Life can still fail; an ordinary Life can develop exceptional ability.
Chapter IV — Legacy Record
Important Legacy receives a dedicated historical record containing, where applicable: Legacy ID, name, origin Civilization, creator/founder, creation date, original purpose, function, development process, effects, social/economic/cultural/political consequences, risks, major events, modifications, current state, and historical status.
Chapter V — Legacy Modification
Important Legacy modifications are versioned. A modification does not erase the previous version. The record preserves who modified it, when, why, what changed, what remained, and what consequences followed.
Chapter VI — History and Civilizational Change
Personal History — history of one Life.
Family History — history of a family/household.
Organization History — history of an organization or faction.
Settlement History — history of a village/town/settlement.
City History — history of a city.
Kingdom History — political-territorial history.
Civilization History — development, spread, transformation, fragmentation, and continuity of a Civilization.
Legacy History — creation, transmission, modification, decline, rediscovery, and survival of important Legacy.
World History — events whose consequences significantly alter the wider world.
The existing History principle remains: every event has a Cause, Process, and Consequence. Existing Canon already states that every Choice creates History and every History creates Legacy. 
Chapter VII — Major Power Transfers and World History
A major change of political power becomes part of World History when its consequences significantly affect the wider world. This can include major conquests, religious-state transformations, civilizational shifts, migrations, technological changes, or Legacy events.
Chapter VIII — The Laws of Civilization — Revised
Law of Identity — A Civilization must have a recognizable identity.
Law of Continuity — Civilization requires transmission across generations.
Law of Influence — Civilization develops through the spread of ways of life and associated systems.
Law of Territory — Civilization and political territory are separate.
Law of Cooperation — Civilization is produced by many Lives and organizations.
Law of Resources — Resources create opportunities but do not determine destiny.
Law of Transformation — Political change does not automatically erase existing society.
Law of Knowledge — Knowledge spreads through realistic transmission.
Law of Legacy — Civilizations leave inheritances that can survive political collapse.
Law of Balance — Greater power creates greater consequences.
Law of History — Major change follows cause → process → consequence.
Law of Renewal — Collapse can become the foundation of new forms of life.
PART VII — HISTORY, LEGACY & CONTINUITY
Chapter I — Great Cycle of History
Choice → Action → Event → History → Legacy → Future Choice.
The original World Bible establishes that Legacy continues to influence the future. 
Chapter II — Historical Memory
History records what actually happened. Legend records how communities remember or retell what happened. They may differ. Forgotten History can disappear from common memory while traces remain in ruins, artifacts, records, names, languages, or traditions.
Chapter III — Continuity of Society
Political replacement does not equal cultural replacement. The simulator must preserve continuity unless evidence and causal events produce change.
PART VIII — CANON RULES
Master Canon Rules
Vendrith is a living-world simulation, not a conventional character-centered game.
The player is one Life among many.
The world continues without the player.
Every Life has value.
Fate is potential, not absolute destiny.
Choice creates consequence.
Growth requires time.
Nothing changes without a believable cause.
Kingdom and Civilization are separate concepts.
Civilizational influence may cross political borders.
Political conquest does not automatically erase society.
Major power changes create historical consequences.
Legacy is persistent and important Legacy is versioned.
Knowledge spreads through realistic transmission.
International language can emerge naturally without replacing native languages.
Vendrith's baseline technology remains medieval fantasy.
Every system — database, engine, UI, AI, wiki, simulator, and novel — follows this World Bible as the Single Source of Truth.
PART IX — REVISION CONTROL
Version 1.1 Change Log
Final Audit Statement
The master now incorporates the cross-reference corrections identified in the audit. The old Civilization growth chain is retained only as a settlement/political development model and no longer functions as the definition of Civilization. Civilization is now an independent, cross-cutting influence layer.
This document is intentionally marked CANON CANDIDATE rather than permanently frozen. The next validation stage is a World Bible → Database/Engine Architecture Audit. That audit will test whether every Canon concept can be represented cleanly in the simulator without contradictory relationships.
SOURCE BASIS
The master consolidation is grounded in the File Library World Bible and the completed cross-reference audit. The original World Bible establishes the living-world philosophy, Fate Grade as potential rather than guarantee, the hierarchy of existence, the Civilization philosophy, the History continuity rule, and the Single Source of Truth rule.

# 2. CANON-TO-ARCHITECTURE AUDIT


VANDRITH WORLD BIBLE
v1.1 — DATABASE & ENGINE ARCHITECTURE AUDIT
Audit #2 — CANON → IMPLEMENTATION
1. Executive Result
The World Bible v1.1 can be implemented as a simulator architecture without requiring the Canon to be redesigned. The key architectural decision is to keep three different dimensions separate: physical/social settlement structure, political sovereignty, and civilizational influence.
The database must not model Civilization as the parent of Kingdom, nor Kingdom as the parent of Civilization. Instead, Civilization is a many-to-many influence layer connected through memberships, cultural influence, language, belief, knowledge, technology, institutions, and Legacy.
2. The Three-Layer Structural Model
Settlement Layer — Camp → Village → Town → City → Capital. Describes physical/social settlement development.
Political Layer — Kingdom, State, Republic, Religious State, City-State, etc. Describes sovereignty, government, laws, administration, and territory.
Civilization Layer — Civilization identity and influence. Describes culture, language, belief, knowledge, traditions, technology, institutions, and Legacy across generations and borders.
This is the most important result of the audit. It prevents the old Civilization/Kingdom hierarchy conflict from reappearing in the database.
3. Canon Entity Mapping
4. Mandatory Database Boundaries
Do not create civilization_id as a mandatory parent foreign key on Kingdom.
Do not create kingdom_id as a mandatory parent foreign key on Civilization.
Use relationship tables for Civilization ↔ Kingdom influence/membership.
Use relationship/history tables for Life ↔ Family, Life ↔ Organization, Life ↔ Religion, and Life ↔ Culture.
Settlement should own physical location/state; polity should own sovereignty/government; Civilization should own or reference influence/identity data.
History events should reference scope/type rather than duplicating separate event systems for every entity.
Legacy should have immutable identity plus versioned records for major modifications.
Fate values should store potential/affinity and provenance, not predetermined outcomes.
Knowledge should track acquisition/transmission state rather than simply granting all knowledge globally.
5. Recommended Core Database Domains
6. Engine Responsibility Audit
7. Event Architecture
The existing Activity Engine design already uses explicit events and ordering. The audit confirms this is the correct direction for the wider simulator.
life:entity:born
life:entity:died
time:tick:completed
time:day:changed
world:weather:changed
world:location:changed
energy:state:changed
energy:fatigue:critical
system:shutdown:requested
Future domains should publish domain events rather than directly reaching into unrelated engine state. A political power transfer, major religious transformation, Civilization change, or Legacy modification should become a history-producing event.
8. History Architecture
Use one generic historical event model with scope and participants rather than separate incompatible history tables for every level.
event_id
event_type
scope_type
scope_id
timestamp
cause_reference
process_reference
consequence_reference
actor_ids
location_id
affected_entity_ids
visibility/known_by
severity/significance
created_at
The exact schema can be finalized during implementation. The important Canon rule is that History records cause → process → consequence.
9. Civilization Data Model
A Civilization should have its own identity record plus relationship tables. Recommended conceptual structure:
civilization
civilization_culture
civilization_language
civilization_religion
civilization_knowledge
civilization_technology
civilization_territory_influence
civilization_polity_relationship
civilization_legacy
civilization_history
These are conceptual domains, not a requirement to create every table immediately. The architecture should allow them without forcing unnecessary complexity into v0.1.
10. Kingdom / Polity Data Model
polity
polity_type
polity_leader
polity_territory
polity_law
polity_faction
polity_diplomacy
polity_history
A polity can have a Church of Light faction and may later transform into a religious state. The transformation should update political state and generate History; it should not rewrite the Civilization identity of the population automatically.
11. Knowledge Model
Knowledge must not be a simple boolean such as knows_magic=true. It should support gradual learning and transmission.
knowledge_id
knowledge_type
complexity/level
prerequisites
source/discovery
teacher_or_institution
holder
mastery/proficiency
transmission_method
availability
historical_origin
This is especially important for the one-year simulator. NPCs should learn, forget, teach, and transmit knowledge through actual relationships and activities.
12. Legacy Model
legacy_id
origin_type / origin_id
creator_or_creators
creation_time
purpose
effects
risk
current_version
legacy_versions
modification_history
major_events
current_status
inheritance/transmission
Major modifications create historical records rather than overwriting the past.
13. Fate Model
Fate should be represented as potential/affinity data attached to a Life. The simulator must not use Fate as a hidden command that forces an outcome.
potential/grade
talent_affinities
opportunity modifiers
heritage/environment factors
development history
actual skill outcome
This preserves the Canon rule: Fate opens possibility; Life, opportunity, effort, time, and choice determine what actually happens.
14. NPC Architecture Implication
An NPC should not contain an entire miniature world inside its own record. The NPC references authoritative domain state.
Identity → Life
Location → World/Settlement
Needs/Energy → Energy
Schedule → Activity
Knowledge → Knowledge
Relationships → Life/Social
Culture/Belief → Civilization/Culture/Religion
Employment → Organization/Activity
Political allegiance → Organization/Polity
History → History
Legacy → Legacy
Fate potential → Life/Fate
15. One-Year Simulation Requirement
The architecture can support a one-year simulation, but one-year simulation should be treated as a stress test of Time, Life, Activity, Energy, World, History, and Save rather than as a requirement to finish every planned engine first.
Year progression must be deterministic enough to reproduce important outcomes.
Births, deaths, travel, work, rest, relationships, economy, weather, and major events must continue without player presence.
History must aggregate important events rather than recording every trivial internal operation as World History.
NPC simulation must have scalable update frequency so 50–100 starting NPCs are manageable on the target hardware.
Save/Load must eventually preserve the state required to resume the year without corrupting causality.
16. v0.1 Scope Recommendation
For the planned beginner village, do not implement the full Civilization/Kingdom simulation immediately. Keep the Canon in the database model, but activate only the minimum necessary state.
World
Settlement
Life
Family
Organization/basic roles
Culture/basic identity
Religion/basic identity
Knowledge/basic learning
Time
Energy
Activity
History
Basic Legacy
Advanced diplomacy, large-scale Kingdom politics, complex Civilization propagation, advanced technology trees, and full Legacy modification networks can remain dormant until the simulator requires them.
17. Contradiction / Risk Register
18. Audit Verdict
ARCHITECTURE: CONDITIONAL PASS.
The World Bible does not require another conceptual rewrite before database work. The critical architectural rule is separation of Settlement, Political, and Civilization layers. With that boundary enforced, the existing Time, World, Life, Energy, and Activity engine direction remains compatible.
The next implementation step should therefore be a Database Schema Blueprint, followed by a Domain Ownership/Event Contract Blueprint. Only after those are stable should the simulator database be populated at scale.
19. Canon Lock Recommendation
World Bible v1.1 remains CANON CANDIDATE. Do not permanently lock it until the database schema blueprint demonstrates that every required relationship can be represented without violating the Canon. After schema validation, perform a final Canon-to-Engine contract audit.
20. Final Architecture Principle
WORLD BIBLE → DOMAIN MODEL → DATABASE SCHEMA → ENGINE CONTRACTS → ENGINE IMPLEMENTATION → SIMULATOR DATA → UI
Never reverse this dependency by allowing an implementation shortcut to redefine Canon.

# 3. DATABASE SCHEMA BLUEPRINT v0.1


VANDRITH DATABASE
DATABASE SCHEMA BLUEPRINT v0.1
Beginner Village Simulator Foundation
1. Design Philosophy
This blueprint translates the World Bible into a database foundation without implementing the entire world at once. The database is designed to be small enough for v0.1 but structurally expandable.
The central rule is: one authoritative owner for each state domain. NPCs reference domain state; they do not duplicate it.
The World Bible remains the Single Source of Truth. The database cannot redefine Canon.
2. v0.1 Scope
World and geographic hierarchy
One beginner settlement: Crescent Moon Village
50–100 initial Lives/NPCs
Families and households
Basic relationships
Organizations and occupations
Time and calendar
Energy/fatigue
Activities, schedules and travel
Basic inventory hooks
Historical events
Basic Legacy hooks
Civilization, complex Kingdom politics, advanced diplomacy, full education institutions, complex Legacy networks, quests, dialogue, and advanced NPC AI are schema-ready but not required to be fully active in v0.1.
3. Domain Dependency Map
Recommended dependency direction:
WORLD → SETTLEMENT → LIFE → SOCIAL → ORGANIZATION → ACTIVITY → HISTORY
TIME is a shared authority used by all simulation domains.
ENERGY is a Life-state authority consumed by Activity.
SAVE persists authoritative state but does not own the rules.
4. World Domain
5. Settlement Domain
Settlement is a physical/social structure, not a Civilization or Kingdom.
6. Life Domain
7. Family & Social Domain
households — living unit, residence, household type, current members
family_groups — long-term kinship identity
family_memberships — life_id, family_id, relation_type, start/end
relationships — life_a, life_b, relationship_type, strength, status, start/end
communities — local social groups
community_memberships — life/community relationship
Do not encode relationships as columns such as mother_id, father_id, spouse_id for every possible relation. Use relationship records so the model can support complex families, adoption, remarriage, friendship, rivalry, mentorship, and future social structures.
8. Organization & Occupation Domain
organizations — guilds, churches, businesses, institutions, factions
organization_memberships — life_id, organization_id, role_id, start/end
roles — role definition and permissions
occupations — occupation definition
employment — life_id, organization_id, occupation_id, start/end, status
A tavern is a building/service/business. A trader visiting for several days is a Life/organization relationship plus a temporary activity/location state. A teacher visiting the village is handled similarly.
9. Time Domain
simulation_clock — world_id, current_tick, current_date, speed, paused
calendar_definitions — calendar rules
time_events — scheduled events
day_records — optional daily aggregate records
Time Engine remains the authoritative source of temporal progression. Other systems consume time; they do not create their own clocks.
10. Energy Domain
life_energy — life_id, current_energy, max_energy, fatigue, state
energy_history — life_id, timestamp, old_state, new_state, cause
Energy is kept separate from the general Life record so the Energy Engine can update it without turning the Life table into a constantly changing catch-all.
11. Activity Domain
activity_definitions — work, sleep, eat, travel, socialize, study, trade, etc.
activities — actual activity instance, actor, start/end, state
schedules — recurring schedule definitions
schedule_entries — time windows and activity references
travel_records — origin, destination, departure, arrival, actor
activity_interruptions — interruption cause and resolution
The Activity Engine owns execution. Activities consume Time and may consume Energy. Completion publishes events.
12. Inventory Hook
items — item definitions
item_instances — individual/stacked item state
containers — household, building, character, shop, etc.
inventory_entries — owner/container + item + quantity
Inventory is included only as a schema hook in v0.1. The full Inventory Engine can be implemented later.
13. History Domain
One generic event model is preferred over separate incompatible history tables.
history_events — id, event_type, scope_type, scope_id, timestamp
history_causes — event_id, cause_type, cause_reference
history_consequences — event_id, consequence_type, consequence_reference
history_participants — event_id, entity_type, entity_id, role
history_locations — event_id, location_id
Major events should capture Cause → Process → Consequence. Not every trivial internal tick becomes World History.
14. Legacy Hook
legacies — identity, origin, creator, purpose, creation_time, current_status
legacy_versions — legacy_id, version_number, state, created_at, reason
legacy_modifications — legacy_id, old_version, new_version, modifier, reason, history_event_id
legacy_links — legacy_id to Life/Organization/Civilization/Settlement/Polity
Legacy versions are append-only in principle. A modification creates a new version instead of destroying historical information.
15. Civilization / Polity Schema Hooks
These domains are not fully activated for village simulation, but their relationships must not be structurally impossible.
civilizations — identity and civilizational metadata
cultures — culture definitions
languages — language definitions
religions — belief/religious institutions
civilization_influences — civilization_id + target_type + target_id + strength/time
polities — political entities
polity_memberships/influences — relationships between Lives, Organizations, Civilizations and Polities
Civilization must NOT require a kingdom_id. Polity must NOT require a civilization_id.
16. Core Relationship Diagram
Conceptual relationship:
World → Continent → Region → Location → Settlement
Settlement → Buildings → Services
Settlement → Households → Lives
Life ↔ Life (Relationships)
Life → Organization Membership → Organization
Life → Employment → Occupation
Life → Schedule → Activity
Activity → Time + Energy + Location
Activity/Event → History
History → Legacy
Civilization ↔ Culture/Language/Religion/Knowledge/Polity/Legacy through relationships
17. Authority Rules
Time Engine owns current simulation time.
World Engine owns geographic/world state.
Life Engine owns Life lifecycle.
Energy Engine owns energy/fatigue state.
Activity Engine owns activity execution.
Inventory Engine owns item ownership/state.
NPC AI proposes actions; domain engines validate and execute them.
History records significant state changes.
Save Engine persists state but never becomes the authority for gameplay rules.
18. Event Contract — v0.1
time:tick:completed
time:day:changed
life:entity:born
life:entity:died
world:location:changed
world:weather:changed
energy:state:changed
energy:fatigue:critical
activity:started
activity:completed
activity:interrupted
travel:started
travel:arrived
relationship:changed
organization:joined
organization:left
history:event:created
legacy:created
legacy:modified
Event names are proposed contracts for the schema/engine phase. They are not yet final API names.
19. Crescent Moon Village v0.1 Data Plan
The database should initially contain one village located at the edge of a dangerous forest. The village can begin with approximately 50–100 Lives without requiring every possible system to be active.
1 World
1 Continent
1 Region
1 Village
Core village buildings
Initial households
50–100 initial Lives
Basic occupations
Basic organizations
Basic relationships
Village resources including the planned small variable mine
Tavern and temporary visitor support
Schedules and activities
Time/calendar
Energy
History
Basic Legacy records
20. Dynamic Population Model
The database must allow the population to change after initialization.
Birth creates a new Life and historical event.
Death ends the Life and creates a historical event.
Migration can move a Life/household into or out of the settlement.
Temporary visitors can exist without becoming permanent residents.
Marriage can create or modify household structure.
Traveling traders can stay for a limited duration.
Professional teachers or specialists can temporarily enter the village.
New families can migrate into the village.
Political/religious changes can influence the village without rewriting every resident's identity.
21. Data Integrity Rules
Foreign keys must protect domain relationships.
Historical records should not be silently deleted when the current state changes.
Important timestamps use the simulation clock rather than device time.
Use status fields for lifecycle state instead of deleting meaningful entities.
Use unique IDs for every persistent entity.
Prefer normalized relationships for many-to-many and time-bounded relationships.
Do not duplicate authoritative values across multiple tables unless a snapshot/cache is explicitly defined.
Use transactions for multi-table state changes that must be atomic.
22. Performance Rules for 50–100 NPCs
Do not run every NPC decision at maximum frequency.
Use Activity/Schedule execution for predictable behavior.
Use event-driven updates where possible.
Aggregate low-value historical data.
Separate authoritative state from derived/cache data.
Use indexes on location_id, household_id, organization_id, activity state, and simulation timestamps.
Design for 100 NPCs first, but avoid schema decisions that make 1,000+ NPCs impossible later.
23. Security & Persistence
Database permissions should prevent client-side users from arbitrarily rewriting authoritative simulation state.
Server/engine-side operations should perform important state transitions.
Save snapshots should be versioned.
World state changes should be recoverable where practical.
History should provide an audit trail for major state changes.
24. Implementation Order
1. worlds / continents / regions / locations
2. settlements / buildings / services / resources
3. lives / attributes / needs / fate
4. households / families / relationships
5. organizations / roles / employment
6. simulation clock
7. energy
8. activities / schedules / travel
9. history
10. basic legacy
11. inventory
12. Civilization/Polity hooks
13. Save Engine
25. What We Should NOT Implement Yet
Full battle system
Complex Kingdom diplomacy
Large-scale Civilization propagation
Advanced AI personality architecture
Full quest system
Full dialogue system
Complex technology tree
Large multi-continent simulation
Hundreds of Legacy variants
These remain compatible with the Canon but should not block the v0.1 simulator.
26. Blueprint Verdict
DATABASE SCHEMA BLUEPRINT v0.1 — APPROVED FOR NEXT DESIGN STAGE.
The conceptual schema is compatible with the World Bible and the Database/Engine Architecture Audit. The next stage is not yet SQL implementation. First we should produce the detailed Table Specification: each table's columns, data types, primary keys, foreign keys, constraints, indexes, status enums, and event relationships.
Only after that detailed specification is approved should we generate the Supabase/PostgreSQL SQL migration.
27. Dependency Chain
World Bible v1.1 Master
↓
Cross-Reference Audit — PASS
↓
Database & Engine Architecture Audit — CONDITIONAL PASS
↓
Database Schema Blueprint v0.1 — APPROVED
↓
NEXT: Detailed Table Specification v0.1
↓
SQL Migration / Supabase Implementation
↓
Seed: Crescent Moon Village + 50–100 Lives
↓
One-Year Simulator Test
28. Source / Canon Basis
This blueprint follows the Master World Bible's Single Source of Truth rule, the living-world philosophy, the separation of Civilization from Kingdom, the cause → process → consequence History model, and the rule that Fate represents potential rather than guaranteed destiny. The architecture audit confirmed these principles can be represented without requiring another conceptual rewrite.
